chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Suleiman al-Dahhan, from Rifa'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, a man from Qays came to Uthman with his slave who had slapped his eye, so water was poured into it, and it remained firm but he could not see anything with it. So he said to him, 'I will give you the blood money,' but he refused.

He said, 'So he sent both of them to Ali (peace be upon him) and said, 'Judge between these two.' So he gave him the blood money, but he refused. He said, 'So they did not cease giving him until they gave him two blood monies.' He said, 'So he said, 'I do not want anything except retaliation (qisas).'

He said, 'So Ali called for a mirror, so he heated it. Then he called for cotton wool, so he moistened it, then placed it on the lids of his eyes and around them. Then he made him face the sun with his eye. He said, 'And he brought the mirror and said, 'Look!' So he looked, and the fat melted, and his eye remained firm, and his vision was gone.'

key_terms.مِرْآة: Mirror (used as a tool for cauterization)

ai.seo_question: What is the procedure for eye retaliation (qisas) in Shia jurisprudence according to Ali (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the principle of *Qisas* (retaliation) in kind, specifically detailing the method of *ta'tir* (cauterization) employed by Imam Ali (AS) to ensure the injury was exact. It highlights the juristic nuance that when the victim rejects monetary compensation (*diyah*), the right to physical retaliation remains, emphasizing the precision required in applying retributive justice. The narrative serves as a key precedent in Shia fiqh for determining the validity of eye injuries and the conditions under which vision loss constitutes a complete retaliation.
